findings.title: Mixing float with flexbox children breaks layout of .small-action
findings.body: `.small-action` was converted to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), but its direct children `.topic-avatar` (line ~270, `float: left;`) and `button` (line ~309, `float: right;`) still rely on `float`. In CSS, `float` is ignored on flex items (direct children of a `display:flex` container). As a result the avatar will no longer be positioned via float but will simply become the first flex item (which happens to look similar), while the `button`'s `float: right` will have no effect at all — it will just be laid out as the last flex item in normal flow instead of being pushed to the right edge of the container. This silently breaks the right-alignment of the action button (e.g. undo/dismiss controls on small-action notices) without any compensating `margin-left: auto` or `justify-content` change. The trailing `clear: both;` on `.small-action` is also now vestigial since there are no floated children to clear within the flex container.

findings.title: Removed `.title { float: left; }` rule without replacement when converting `.contents` to flexbox
findings.body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule nested inside `.d-header .contents` while turning `.contents` into a flex container. No `order` or other flex-specific rule was added for `.title` to replace the old floating behavior, unlike `.panel` which received `margin-left: auto; @include order(3);`. If `.title` is one of the flex items inside `.contents`, its layout now depends entirely on flex default behavior (order 0, normal flex-basis) with no explicit styling, which may differ from the previous floated layout and could shift or resize the site title/logo area unexpectedly.

findings.title: `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` with no visible flex container context
findings.body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now has `@include order(2)` applied, but the CSS `order` property only has an effect on elements that are direct children of a flex (or grid) container. Nothing in this file establishes `.extra-info-wrapper`'s parent as `display: flex`. If the parent element isn't a flex container (and no such change is visible in this PR), this `order` declaration is a no-op and the intended re-ordering will silently fail to take effect, leaving dead/misleading CSS in the stylesheet.

findings.title: Removed `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` inside `.extra-info-wrapper` without equivalent replacement
findings.body: The previous rule gave bullet-style badge wrappers inside `.extra-info-wrapper` a 5px top margin for vertical alignment. This specific rule was deleted and replaced only with a `line-height: 1.5` on the parent `.extra-info-wrapper`. Line-height alone does not reproduce a per-element top margin; depending on surrounding content this can cause the bullet badge to misalign vertically relative to the rest of the extra-info row, since the compensating offset for the bullet variant is gone.
